questions.question: What is the main reason Ethernet requires different physical‑layer protocols for twisted‑pair copper, coaxial cable, and fiber optics?

options.A: To support multiple IP addressing schemes on each medium
options.B: Because each medium has distinct signaling and transmission characteristics requiring tailored physical‑layer specifications
options.C: To enable Ethernet to operate at both layer 2 and layer 3 simultaneously
options.D: To provide encryption uniquely suited to each cable type

questions.explanation:
The context states that Ethernet has many physical‑layer protocols, each designed for a specific transmission medium such as twisted‑pair copper, coaxial cable, or fiber, because the media differ in signaling requirements. [Page 52]

questions.question: What is the key distinction between a link‑layer switch and an Internet router regarding protocol implementation?

options.A: A switch implements TCP, while a router implements UDP
options.B: A switch operates only on wireless links, whereas a router works only on wired links
options.C: A link‑layer switch works with layer‑2 (Ethernet) addresses, while a router implements the layer‑3 IP protocol
options.D: A switch provides end‑to‑end routing, whereas a router only forwards frames within a LAN

questions.explanation:
The text explains that Internet routers are capable of implementing the IP protocol (layer 3), while link‑layer switches recognize layer 2 addresses such as Ethernet addresses. [Page 53]

---

questions.question: What is the difference between reliable delivery offered by certain link‑layer protocols and the reliability provided by TCP?

options.A: Link‑layer reliability ensures delivery over a single hop only, whereas TCP guarantees delivery across the entire path
options.B: TCP provides reliability only for wired links, while link‑layer reliability works only for wireless links
options.C: Link‑layer protocols guarantee packet ordering, while TCP does not
options.D: TCP’s reliability is optional, whereas link‑layer reliability is mandatory on all networks

questions.explanation:
The context notes that some link‑layer protocols provide reliable delivery from transmitting node to receiving node over one link, and that this service differs from TCP’s end‑to‑end reliable delivery. [Page 51]

questions.question: What is an example of a link‑layer protocol that has been standardized by the IEEE 802 LAN Standards Committee?
questions.explanation:
The IEEE 802 LAN Standards Committee specifies Ethernet and WiFi standards, both of which are link‑layer protocols. [Page 5]

questions.question: What is the role of layer‑2 (Ethernet) addresses in link‑layer switches?

options.A: They enable switches to assign IP addresses to hosts
options.B: They allow switches to make forwarding decisions within a local network segment
options.C: They provide end‑to‑end encryption keys for data packets
options.D: They determine the routing path across multiple autonomous systems

questions.explanation:
Link‑layer switches recognize layer 2 addresses, such as Ethernet addresses, to forward frames appropriately. [Page 53]

questions.question: What is the implication of a datagram being handled by different link‑layer protocols (e.g., Ethernet on one link, PPP on another) as it traverses the network?

options.A: The datagram must be converted to a universal format before reaching the destination
options.B: The datagram’s IP header is replaced by a new header at each hop
options.C: The datagram is encapsulated with the appropriate link‑layer header for each individual link, such as Ethernet or PPP
options.D: The datagram loses its original source address when crossing a different link‑layer protocol

questions.explanation:
The passage explains that a datagram may be handled by different link‑layer protocols on different links, meaning it is re‑encapsulated with the appropriate link‑layer header at each hop. [Page 51]

questions.question: What is the analogy used to describe packet‑switched networks, and what aspect does it illustrate?

options.A: It compares data packets to vehicles moving cargo on highways, illustrating routing and forwarding across a network
options.B: It likens packets to water flowing through pipes, emphasizing bandwidth limitations
options.C: It equates packets to letters in a postal system, focusing on address formatting
options.D: It treats packets as musical notes in a symphony, highlighting timing synchronization

questions.explanation:
The text uses the analogy of a factory moving cargo to a distant warehouse via highways to explain packet‑switched networks. [Page 4]

questions.question: What is the primary service that some link‑layer protocols provide, which is not guaranteed by all link‑layer protocols?

options.B: Automatic IP address allocation to hosts
options.D: Reliable delivery of frames over a single link

questions.explanation:
The context notes that certain link‑layer protocols provide reliable delivery from the transmitting node to the receiving node over one link, a service not offered by all link‑layer protocols. [Page 51]

questions.question: What does the mention of nearly 9000 RFCs imply about network standards?

options.A: There are exactly 9000 protocols used in modern networks
options.B: It indicates a large and continuously evolving body of documented protocols and standards
options.C: All RFCs are mandatory for every network device to implement
options.D: The number of RFCs limits the number of possible network topologies

questions.explanation:
The passage states there are currently nearly 9000 RFCs, highlighting the extensive and evolving set of network standards. [Page 5]

questions.question: What is the effect of using different link‑layer protocols on end‑to‑end throughput and delay models discussed in the context?

options.A: Different protocols eliminate the need to consider propagation delay
options.B: All link‑layer protocols produce identical throughput, so models remain unchanged
options.C: Varying transmission rates and overhead of each protocol influence overall end‑to‑end delay and throughput calculations
options.D: Link‑layer protocols only affect security, not performance metrics

questions.explanation: The text mentions quantitative models for end‑to‑end throughput and delay that must account for transmission, propagation, and queuing delays, which can vary with the characteristics of each link‑layer protocol. [Page 2]
